title: Traffic shadowing composer and split-template inspector
creator: Marina Alvarez
description: Goal: Design a composer and inspector flow in the Redwood Console that makes traffic shadowing and traffic-split templating discoverable, safe, and verifiable for staged rollouts. Rationale: Teams want to validate model variants and downstream metrics without exposing users to unstable variants. This ticket focuses on the UX patterns to author shadow-compositions, reuse split templates, preview traffic diffs, and trigger rollback gestures. Scope: 1) Composer canvas to create shadow connections (live-copying a percentage of requests to a variant), 2) Split-template library (named templates for common splits like 90/10, 50/50, stratified by region or key), 3) Inspector panel showing live metrics, divergence signals, cost delta estimator, and simulated rollback outcomes, 4) Sandbox simulator to replay historical traffic and estimate latency/error/cost impacts. Out of scope: backend API and instrumentation work (ENG to own). Acceptance criteria: - High-fidelity Figma screens for composer + inspector + template library - Prototype that simulates traffic for demo (no real-serving modifications) - Design spec with accessibility labels, edge-case flows for emergency rollback, and copy for tooltips and warnings - Stakeholder sign-off from PM, Eng reliability and Security
comments: 2026-02-25 — Marina Alvarez: Kickoff — aligned with PM on goal to make shadowing low-friction. Decided to prioritise composer discoverability over advanced rule-editing for initial prototype.
2026-02-28 — Evan Cho: Early sketches done. Two composer metaphors explored: pipeline graph vs. lane-based composer. Leaning toward lane composer for quick template reuse.
2026-03-02 — Priya Sharma (PM): Please add explicit safety tether (ability to mute shadow traffic completely) and an 'exposure budget' UI that counts live requests sent to variants.

2026-03-04 — Alex Turner (Eng Reliability): Need to show model divergence signals (KL divergence and token-level diffs) and surface when rollback should be recommended. We'll provide metrics endpoints ENG-9120.

2026-03-06 — Design review: Feedback to reduce cognitive load in inspector; move cost estimator to a compact toggle and add contextual help. Also, add a 'simulate rollback' action showing projected user impact.
2026-03-09 — Security review note: Shadowing must be opt-in per project and log access needs to respect RBAC. Security team requests a compact notice in composer and link to audit logs.
2026-03-11 — Marina Alvarez: Prototype completed and linked; preparing demo for product review on 2026-03-15. Next: Handoff ticket to Eng with specs and tokenized visual assets.
